title: Macbeth
author: William Shakespeare
sourceNote: Act 5, Scene 5 — the 'tomorrow and tomorrow' soliloquy
description: Macbeth learns of his wife's death and answers it with the bleakest assessment of life in the play, right before his own end arrives.

title: Hope is the thing with feathers
author: Emily Dickinson
description: A short extended metaphor comparing hope to a bird that never stops singing, never asks anything of you, and never truly leaves.

title: The Tyger
author: William Blake
description: A string of unanswered questions asking what kind of maker could forge something as fearsome and symmetrical as a tiger.

title: Death, be not proud
author: John Donne
description: A direct taunt aimed at Death itself, arguing it has no real power and will one day die too.

title: The Road Not Taken
author: Robert Frost
description: A traveler chooses between two nearly identical paths in a wood and only later decides to tell the story as if the choice mattered more than it did.

title: Ode to a Nightingale
author: John Keats
description: The poet aches at the sound of a nightingale's song and wants to dissolve into it, then is startled back to himself by his own word 'forlorn.'

title: Annabel Lee
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: A narrator insists that his love for a dead girl was so total that even angels and demons cannot separate his soul from hers.

title: O Captain! My Captain!
author: Walt Whitman
sourceNote: Leaves of Grass, written for Lincoln, 1865
description: A sailor realizes, in the middle of a victory celebration, that the captain being cheered for is already dead on the deck beneath him.

title: Ulysses
author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
description: An aging Ulysses, bored on the throne he fought to reclaim, decides to gather his old crew for one last voyage rather than grow old at home.

title: Remember
author: Christina Rossetti
description: A sonnet asking to be remembered after death, which then reverses itself and says forgetting, if it brings a smile instead of grief, is better.

title: Ozymandias
author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
description: A traveler describes a ruined statue in the desert whose inscription boasts of power that has long since turned to sand on every side.

title: Hamlet
author: William Shakespeare
sourceNote: Act 3, Scene 1 — the 'to be, or not to be' soliloquy
description: Hamlet weighs whether the pain of living is worse than the uncertainty of what comes after dying, and concludes that fear of the unknown is what keeps anyone going.

title: Romeo and Juliet
author: William Shakespeare
description: Romeo watches Juliet appear at her window and talks himself into believing she outshines the sun, just before she wonders aloud why he has to be a Montague.

title: Othello
author: William Shakespeare
description: Othello stands over the sleeping Desdemona, talking himself into killing her even as he admits he cannot restore a light once it's out.

title: Twelfth Night
author: William Shakespeare
sourceNote: Act 1, Scene 1 — 'If music be the food of love'
description: Duke Orsino asks for music to feed his lovesickness until it sickens and dies, then immediately asks the musicians to stop.

title: The Importance of Being Earnest
author: Oscar Wilde
sourceNote: Act 1 — Lady Bracknell's interrogation of Jack
description: Lady Bracknell interrogates Jack about his parentage and is horrified to learn he was discovered, as a baby, inside a handbag at a railway station.

title: Doctor Faustus
author: Christopher Marlowe
sourceNote: Act 5, Scene 1 — Faustus and the spirit of Helen
description: Faustus, near the end of his bargain with the devil, kisses the conjured spirit of Helen of Troy and declares he would burn any city for her all over again.

title: A Doll's House
author: Henrik Ibsen
description: Nora returns her wedding ring, explains exactly why she can no longer be anyone's doll, and walks out the door for good.

title: Julius Caesar
author: William Shakespeare
description: Antony claims he has come only to bury Caesar, not to praise him, then spends the rest of the speech turning the crowd against the men who killed him.

title: As You Like It
author: William Shakespeare
sourceNote: Act 2, Scene 7 — 'All the world's a stage'
description: Jaques lays out a life in seven acts, from a mewling infant to a second childhood with no teeth, eyes, taste, or anything else left.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: Mrs. Bennet badgers her husband with news of a rich new neighbor, already certain it means a husband for one of their daughters.

title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
description: Ishmael explains that going to sea is his personal substitute for a more direct kind of self-destruction.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: Jane refuses to be treated as beneath feeling and insists, poor and plain as she is, that her soul and heart are exactly Rochester's equal.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description: Victor Frankenstein watches the creature he spent two years assembling open its dull yellow eye for the first time, and is instantly disgusted by what he's made.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
description: Dorian looks at his own freshly painted portrait and, in a moment of panic about aging, wishes aloud that the picture could grow old instead of him.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
description: A string of contradictions tries to describe an entire age at once, before settling into the ordinary business of two kings and two large jaws.

title: Heart of Darkness
author: Joseph Conrad
description: Marlow watches Kurtz's face change in his final moments as he seems to relive his whole life before crying out his last words.

title: The Yellow Wallpaper
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
description: A woman confined to a rented summer house for her health insists something is wrong with the place, while her husband refuses to believe she's actually sick.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
description: Catherine tries to explain to Nelly why marrying someone else won't change anything, because her bond with Heathcliff isn't a preference but her own being.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description: Jonathan Harker meets Count Dracula for the first time at the castle door, and is unsettled by a handshake as cold as a dead man's.
